questions.stem: A 49-year-old man drank heavily at a party last night and vomited forcefully many times. An hour after the last episode he had sudden, severe pain behind the sternum that spread to his back. Temperature is 38.4°C, blood pressure is 102/64 mm Hg, pulse is 122/min, and respiratory rate is 26/min. The skin over his neck crackles when pressed, and a crunching sound is heard with each heartbeat. A chest x-ray shows air along the borders of the mediastinum and a small left pleural effusion. Which best describes his injury?
choices: Superficial tear of the mucosa at the gastroesophageal junction
Full-thickness tear of the distal esophageal wall
Rupture of a dilated submucosal vein in the distal esophagus
Perforation of an ulcer in the anterior duodenal wall
Tear in the inner layer of the descending aortic wall
questions.explanation: Forceful vomiting followed by chest pain, fever, **subcutaneous emphysema**, a mediastinal crunch and **pneumomediastinum** with a left effusion is **Boerhaave syndrome**: a **transmural rupture**, usually of the left side of the distal esophagus. A **Mallory-Weiss tear** has the same trigger, but it involves only the mucosa, so it causes hematemesis without air in the mediastinum. A perforated duodenal ulcer puts free air under the diaphragm, not in the mediastinum.
questions.explanation_pt: Vômitos intensos seguidos de dor torácica, febre, **enfisema subcutâneo**, crepitação mediastinal sincrônica com os batimentos cardíacos e **pneumomediastino** com derrame à esquerda indicam **síndrome de Boerhaave**: uma **ruptura transmural**, geralmente da parede esquerda do esôfago distal. A **laceração de Mallory-Weiss** tem o mesmo gatilho, mas atinge apenas a mucosa, causando hematêmese sem ar no mediastino. Uma úlcera duodenal perfurada produz ar livre sob o diafragma, e não no mediastino.

questions.stem: A 74-year-old man has 1 year of food sticking in his throat. He often coughs up pieces of food that he ate the day before. His wife says his breath smells bad, and a gurgling sound comes from his neck when he drinks. He has had pneumonia twice this year. A barium swallow shows a contrast-filled pouch behind the lower pharynx, just above the upper esophageal sphincter. The rest of the esophagus is normal. Which best describes this lesion?
choices: True diverticulum pulled outward by scarred lymph nodes
Congenital cyst lined by ciliated or gastric epithelium
Thin mucosal web that narrows the upper esophageal lumen
Mucosa and submucosa herniating through a muscular gap
Dilation of the whole esophagus above a tight sphincter
questions.explanation: Regurgitation of old food, **halitosis**, a gurgling neck and aspiration in an older man point to a **Zenker diverticulum**. It is a **false (pulsion) diverticulum**: high pressure above a poorly relaxing **cricopharyngeus** pushes mucosa and submucosa through a weak area in the **posterior hypopharynx**. A **traction diverticulum** is a true diverticulum of the **mid-esophagus**, pulled out by scarred mediastinal nodes (for example after tuberculosis), and it rarely causes symptoms.
questions.explanation_pt: Regurgitação de alimentos antigos, **halitose**, gorgolejo cervical e aspiração em idoso indicam **divertículo de Zenker**. É um **divertículo falso (de pulsão)**: a pressão alta acima de um **cricofaríngeo** que relaxa mal empurra mucosa e submucosa por uma área fraca na **parede posterior da hipofaringe**. O **divertículo de tração** é um divertículo verdadeiro do **esôfago médio**, puxado por linfonodos mediastinais cicatrizados (por exemplo, após tuberculose), e raramente causa sintomas.

questions.stem: A 47-year-old woman has 6 months of solid food sticking high in her throat. Liquids pass easily. Her menstrual periods are very heavy. Exam shows pale skin, a smooth red tongue, and spoon-shaped fingernails. Laboratory results: hemoglobin 9.2 g/dL, mean corpuscular volume 68 fL, red cell distribution width 18%, and serum ferritin 5 ng/mL. A barium swallow shows a thin shelf of tissue that partly blocks the upper esophagus, just below the cricopharyngeus. This condition increases her risk of which cancer?
choices: Squamous cell carcinoma of the upper esophagus
Adenocarcinoma of the lower esophagus
Diffuse-type gastric adenocarcinoma with signet-ring cells
Gastrointestinal stromal tumor of the stomach
Extranodal marginal zone lymphoma of the stomach
questions.explanation: Dysphagia, **iron deficiency anemia** (microcytic, low ferritin, high RDW) and an **upper esophageal web** form **Plummer-Vinson syndrome**; glossitis and koilonychia are common. It raises the risk of **squamous cell carcinoma** of the **hypopharynx and upper esophagus**. **Esophageal adenocarcinoma** is tempting, but it arises in the **lower third** from **Barrett esophagus** caused by chronic reflux, not from webs.
questions.explanation_pt: Disfagia, **anemia ferropriva** (microcítica, ferritina baixa, RDW alto) e uma **membrana (*web*) no esôfago superior** formam a **síndrome de Plummer-Vinson**; glossite e coiloníquia são comuns. Ela aumenta o risco de **carcinoma espinocelular** da **hipofaringe e do esôfago superior**. O **adenocarcinoma de esôfago** é tentador, mas surge no **terço inferior** a partir do **esôfago de Barrett** causado por refluxo crônico, e não de membranas.

questions.stem: A 23-year-old man comes to the emergency department because a piece of steak is stuck in his chest. Over the past 2 years food has stuck several times, and he now cuts his food into very small pieces. He has asthma, eczema, and a peanut allergy. He has no heartburn and no history of immunodeficiency. The bolus is removed by endoscopy. The esophagus shows stacked circular rings along its full length, linear furrows, and small white specks. Biopsies are taken from the upper and lower esophagus. What is the most likely biopsy finding?
choices: Columnar epithelium with goblet cells in the distal esophagus
Yeast forms and pseudohyphae in white plaques
Multinucleated squamous cells with intranuclear inclusions
Loss of ganglion cells in the myenteric plexus
Many eosinophils within the squamous epithelium
questions.explanation: An atopic young man with recurrent **food impaction** and stacked rings (*trachealization*) with furrows along the whole esophagus has **eosinophilic esophagitis**, a **Th2-driven** allergic reaction to food antigens. Biopsies from both the upper and lower esophagus show **dense intraepithelial eosinophils**. The white specks are eosinophil microabscesses, not **Candida**; candidal plaques are typical in immunocompromised patients and cause pain on swallowing rather than recurrent impaction.
questions.explanation_pt: Um homem jovem e atópico com **impactação alimentar** recorrente e anéis empilhados (*traquealização*) com sulcos ao longo de todo o esôfago tem **esofagite eosinofílica**, uma reação alérgica a antígenos alimentares **mediada por Th2**. As biópsias do esôfago superior e inferior mostram **muitos eosinófilos intraepiteliais**. Os pontos brancos são microabscessos eosinofílicos, e não **Candida**; as placas por cândida são típicas de imunocomprometidos e causam dor ao engolir, e não impactação recorrente.

questions.stem: A 36-year-old man with HIV who stopped antiretroviral therapy 2 years ago has 3 weeks of severe pain when he swallows and low-grade fever. His CD4 count is 32/μL. One week of fluconazole did not help. Endoscopy shows a few large, shallow, long ulcers in the distal esophagus. There are no white plaques. Biopsies are taken from the base of the ulcers. What is the most likely biopsy finding?
choices: Yeast forms and pseudohyphae in a pseudomembrane
Multinucleated squamous cells with intranuclear inclusions
Enlarged endothelial cells with intranuclear inclusions
Dense eosinophils within intact squamous epithelium
Columnar epithelium with goblet cells in the distal esophagus
questions.explanation: Large, shallow **linear ulcers** in a patient with a very low CD4 count, no plaques and no response to fluconazole suggest **CMV esophagitis**. CMV infects **endothelial and stromal cells** in the ulcer base, which become large and show a large **intranuclear inclusion** with a clear halo (*owl's eye*) and smaller **cytoplasmic inclusions**. **HSV** is the most tempting distractor, but it makes small **punched-out ulcers**, and its multinucleated squamous cells with molded nuclei sit at the ulcer **edge**, not the base.
questions.explanation_pt: **Úlceras lineares** grandes e rasas em paciente com CD4 muito baixo, sem placas e sem resposta ao fluconazol sugerem **esofagite por CMV**. O CMV infecta **células endoteliais e estromais** da base da úlcera, que ficam aumentadas e mostram uma grande **inclusão intranuclear** com halo claro (*olho de coruja*) e pequenas **inclusões citoplasmáticas**. O **HSV** é a alternativa mais tentadora, mas causa **úlceras pequenas, em saca-bocado**, e suas células escamosas multinucleadas com núcleos moldados ficam na **borda** da úlcera, e não na base.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman has 3 months of early satiety, vomiting, and an 8-kg weight loss. Endoscopy shows a thick, stiff stomach wall that does not expand when air is blown in. There is no discrete mass or ulcer. Biopsy shows single cells scattered through the wall; each cell has a large mucin vacuole that pushes the nucleus to the side. Her father died of stomach cancer at age 41, and her paternal aunt had lobular breast cancer at age 45. A germline mutation in which gene is most likely?
choices: APC
CDH1
MLH1
BRCA2
TP53
questions.explanation: **Signet-ring cells** infiltrating a rigid stomach (**linitis plastica**) are **diffuse-type gastric adenocarcinoma**. Loss of **E-cadherin**, encoded by **CDH1**, lets tumor cells detach and spread one by one; germline CDH1 mutations cause hereditary diffuse gastric cancer and **lobular breast cancer**. **BRCA2** is tempting because of the breast cancer, but it mainly causes ductal breast, ovarian, prostate and pancreatic cancer, not diffuse gastric cancer. **MLH1** (Lynch) is linked to intestinal-type gastric cancer.
questions.explanation_pt: **Células em anel de sinete** infiltrando um estômago rígido (**linite plástica**) indicam **adenocarcinoma gástrico do tipo difuso**. A perda de **E-caderina**, codificada pelo **CDH1**, permite que as células tumorais se soltem e se espalhem uma a uma; mutações germinativas em CDH1 causam câncer gástrico difuso hereditário e **carcinoma lobular de mama**. O **BRCA2** é tentador por causa do câncer de mama, mas causa principalmente câncer de mama ductal, de ovário, de próstata e de pâncreas, e não câncer gástrico difuso. O **MLH1** (Lynch) está ligado ao câncer gástrico do tipo intestinal.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old man is in the intensive care unit after a motorcycle crash with a severe head injury. CT shows a large subdural hematoma with midline shift. He has no burns, and his blood pressure has never been low. He took no medications before the crash. On day 3, coffee-ground material appears in his nasogastric tube. Current vital signs: blood pressure 178/96 mm Hg, pulse 50/min, and irregular breathing. Endoscopy shows one deep ulcer in the upper stomach. Which mechanism best explains this ulcer?
choices: Mucosal ischemia from low circulating blood volume
Inhibition of mucosal prostaglandin synthesis
Gastrin release from a neuroendocrine tumor
Increased vagal stimulation of parietal cells
Urease-producing bacteria in the gastric mucus
questions.explanation: Hypertension, bradycardia and irregular breathing (the **Cushing reflex**) show raised **intracranial pressure**. An ulcer that forms after brain injury is a **Cushing ulcer**: stimulation of the **vagal nuclei** increases acetylcholine release onto **parietal cells**, so acid secretion rises. **Mucosal ischemia from hypovolemia** is the mechanism of a **Curling ulcer** after severe burns, but this patient has no burns and has never been hypotensive.
questions.explanation_pt: Hipertensão, bradicardia e respiração irregular (**reflexo de Cushing**) indicam **hipertensão intracraniana**. Uma úlcera que surge após lesão cerebral é uma **úlcera de Cushing**: o estímulo dos **núcleos vagais** aumenta a liberação de acetilcolina sobre as **células parietais**, e a secreção ácida sobe. A **isquemia da mucosa por hipovolemia** é o mecanismo da **úlcera de Curling** após grandes queimaduras, mas este paciente não tem queimaduras e nunca esteve hipotenso.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old man has 4 months of epigastric fullness, nausea, and a 6-kg weight loss. His ankles have become swollen. He drinks no alcohol and takes no medications. Exam shows pitting edema to the mid-shins. Laboratory results: serum albumin 2.2 g/dL, urine dipstick negative for protein, AST 22 U/L, ALT 19 U/L, total bilirubin 0.6 mg/dL, INR 1.0, and normal stool fat. Endoscopy shows very large, thick folds in the gastric body and fundus; the antrum is normal. Biopsy shows marked hyperplasia of surface mucous cells with long, twisted pits and few parietal cells. Gastric acid output is low. What is the most likely cause of his low serum albumin?
choices: Loss of albumin in the urine
Reduced albumin synthesis in the liver
Loss of protein across the gastric mucosa
Malabsorption of amino acids in the small bowel
Protein loss from dilated intestinal lymphatics
questions.explanation: Giant rugal folds in the body and fundus, **foveolar (surface mucous cell) hyperplasia**, fewer parietal cells and **low acid** are **Ménétrier disease**. The hyperplastic mucosa leaks protein into the stomach, so it is a **protein-losing gastropathy** that causes hypoalbuminemia and edema. A negative dipstick argues against **nephrotic syndrome**, and normal INR and bilirubin argue against **liver failure**. Zollinger-Ellison syndrome can also thicken the folds, but it raises acid output instead of lowering it.
questions.explanation_pt: Pregas gástricas gigantes no corpo e no fundo, **hiperplasia foveolar (das células mucosas de superfície)**, menos células parietais e **pouco ácido** indicam **doença de Ménétrier**. A mucosa hiperplásica perde proteína para dentro do estômago, caracterizando uma **gastropatia perdedora de proteínas** que causa hipoalbuminemia e edema. A fita reagente urinária negativa para proteína vai contra **síndrome nefrótica**, e INR e bilirrubina normais vão contra **insuficiência hepática**. A síndrome de Zollinger-Ellison também espessa as pregas, mas aumenta a produção de ácido em vez de reduzi-la.
